story:
It was a sunny day at Sunnydale Elementary School. The playground was buzzing with excited chatter and the sound of kids playing on the swings. Soomin, a happy five-year-old, was sitting in his classroom, eagerly waiting for lunchtime to arrive.

As he opened his brand-new lunchbox, which his mom had bought him just yesterday, he exclaimed, "Wow! Look at all these yummy sandwiches!" But as he reached for the top sandwich, he realized with a big frown that his lunchbox was nowhere to be found!

"Oh no!" Soomin cried out. "My lunchbox is lost!"

Mrs. Thompson, their kind teacher, came over and asked, "What's wrong, Soomin?" Soomin explained how he couldn't find his lunchbox. Mrs. Thompson said, "Don't worry, we'll find it together! Let's ask the class if they've seen it."

The class started searching high and low, calling out to each other, "Has anyone seen Soomin's lunchbox?!" Their friend Emma, who was sitting next to Soomin, shouted, "Oh, I saw something shiny on the playground! Maybe that's your lunchbox!"

Soomin and his friends ran outside to investigate. They found a small box peeking out from under a big tree. It was Soomin's lunchbox! But oh no, it was covered in mud!

The kids cheered, "Yay! We found it!" Mrs. Thompson said, "Great job working together, everyone! Now let's clean up this muddy lunchbox." Emma suggested using the water bottle to wash off the mud.

As they washed and dried Soomin's lunchbox, he realized that helping his friends find his lost item was much more fun than just eating his sandwiches alone. He felt happy that his friends were there to support him.

When lunchtime arrived, Mrs. Thompson handed out yummy sandwiches from a big basket. As they ate together, Soomin said with a smile, "I'm so glad I have such great friends! They helped me find my lost lunchbox."

Mrs. Thompson smiled and said, "That's what friends are for! We're all happy to help each other out." The kids clapped and cheered, feeling happy and content.
